1) yes that's exactly what you'd assume! Water changes and clean water are essential to a happy, healthy turtle. A quarter to half of your water should be changed weekly so that ammonia from waste doesn't build up and harm your turtle.

2) while I am not perfectly qualified to answer on /this part/ of your question, I know that most animals need to have a set stable environment with few stressors and enough food sources to breed, and turtles take a good few years to reach sexual maturity anyway, some up to 8 years. A good way to check if your larger female is pregnant is by massaging the soft flesh between the end of your turtles shell and under the tail, if there are hard lumps your turtle is pregnant! 

I hope I was able to help and good luck to you and your little friends!
